messages.subject: summary obs. error responses
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,
This a summary of responses I received regarding how to try and correct for
an observer who had underestimated distances for the first two years of
data when data were collected in intervals.

1)If I was going to use the data from the previous two years I would need
to check that there were no significant year to year differences.  In other
words if the year with the good data was a lot different than the other
years for some reason than I can=92t use the data from the good year to
correct the not so good years.

2)Using a multiplier might effectively being doing the same thing as using
the 3rd year of data to correct the first two: ( this is probably what I am
going to do)
=93This is effectively chucking out the distance data from the 1st 2 years
and just keeping the encounter rate info.=94

3) if the observer was consistently underestimating distances than I could
change the cutpoints on the intervals.  =93 For example if the estimate was
0.8 the real distances, cutpoints of 0, 50 and 100 meters would become 0,
62.6 and 125 meters.=94

Things get a little more complicated because I=92m bootstrapping to obtain
variance estimates, so I can either a) use a pre-calculated multiplier or
cut off point for the observer if he comes up in the bootstrap or b)
recalculate the correction every time I do a bootstrap (which incorporates
uncertainty due to the correction in the variance estimate)

Thanks to those who responded.  Any more comments on the above are welcome.

Robin Russell
Postdoctoral Ecologist
Rocky Mountain Research Station
Bozeman, MT 59717
reru...@fs.fed.us
